label: prf:two-filtration-bridge-general
title: Proof of two filtration bridge general
html:
Proof. Proof of two filtration bridge general

Proof — bar-eigenspace argument

Step 1 (bar action on central idempotents). The bar involution acts on the central primitive idempotent e_\lambda \in Z(H_n(q)) (prop:explicit-central-idempotent, prop:hecke-baer-star-generic) by

  \mathrm{bar}(e_\lambda) \;=\; e_{\lambda'},

where \lambda' is the transpose Young diagram.

Step 2 (period-class bar-action). Under the archimedean realization functor \tau_{\mathrm{arch}} (def:archimedean-realization-functor), the bar involution acts on the period side by:

  • Hyperbolic volume: \mathrm{Vol}(K) = \mathrm{Vol}(\overline{K}) — bar-INVARIANT (orientation-reversal preserves the metric). Lives in \mathcal{P}_2^+ (real, bar-fixed).
  • Chern–Simons: \mathrm{CS}(K) = -\mathrm{CS}(\overline{K}) mod \pi^2 \mathbb{Z} — bar-ANTI-INVARIANT (CS picks up the orientation sign). Lives in \mathcal{P}_3^- (Tate-twisted).

These are the two characteristic period-class bar-types at depths 2 and 3 respectively.

Step 3 (pairing analysis).

Self-conjugate case \lambda = \lambda'. \mathrm{bar}(e_\lambda) = e_\lambda — the cell is bar-fixed. Pairing with a depth-n grouplike g \in G^{(n)}(\mathcal{H}_q) under Markov trace yields a value in the bar-fixed component of \mathcal{P}_n / \mathcal{P}_{n - 1}:

  • At n = 2: pairs with \mathrm{Vol} (bar-fixed) — non-by definition.
  • At n = 3: pairs with \mathrm{CS} (bar-anti-fixed) — gives zero on bar-fixed cells.

So bar-fixed cell \Rightarrow d_{\mathrm{II}}(\lambda) = 2.

Chiral pair case \lambda \neq \lambda'. \mathrm{bar}(e_\lambda) = e_{\lambda'} — bar swaps the two cells. The bar-eigenspaces of the direct sum e_\lambda + e_{\lambda'} decompose as:

  • Bar-symmetric: (e_\lambda + e_{\lambda'})/2 — pairs with depth-2 (Vol-type) periods.
  • Bar-antisymmetric: (e_\lambda - e_{\lambda'})/2 — pairs with depth-3 (CS-type) periods non-by definition.

The bar-symmetric part pairs by definition with depth-2 of a chiral knot (volume can be non-zero, but in the chiral pair the antisymmetric content carries the orientation-dependent signature). The bar-antisymmetric part is the natural pairing partner of \mathrm{CS} (which is bar-anti-invariant).

So chiral pair \Rightarrow d_{\mathrm{II}}(\lambda) = 3.

\square

Generality of the proof

The argument is structural, not case-by-case:

  1. No upper bound on n. Works for partitions of any size.
  2. Bar-class of \lambda is computable. Self-conjugate partitions of n are exactly those with bar-fixed Young diagram (a well-defined combinatorial property).
  3. Depth assignment is binary. Either 2 or 3 — no other values arise in this bridge.

See Table.

(Self-conjugate partitions of n are in bijection with partitions of n into distinct odd parts — a classical result.)
